  -V, --version                            output the version number

  spec-check [options] <spec...>           deterministic spec conformance: every acceptance criterion is LINKED to a present delivered artifact, and every criterion identifier the bundle references is declared — never a claim it is semantically met (ADR-0056)
  status [options]                         where am I — mission snapshot: current gate, decision journal, workflows
  doctor [options]                         environment and installation checks
  wire [options]                           recommend the auto-trigger channel for the AI harness running this command (read-only without --install; --install, run by the operator in a terminal, arms the gate — ADR-0065)
  update [options]                         refresh runward/workflows/ and runward/rules/ from this package version (mission state untouched)
  characterize [options]                   inventory of an existing codebase (brownfield/retro-doc): never modifies your code; writes runward/characterization.md, and runward/adr/DRAFT-*.md with --mine
  manifest [options]                       rule-conformance manifest overview; --sync scaffolds missing rows and migrates renamed slugs (form only, never content)
  propose [options]                        deterministic proposer: fill empty manifest rows as proposed:applied where a rule's signature matches inside its declared territory — no model call; the gate refuses every proposal until it is ratified (runward ADR-0066)
  ratify [options]                         turn proposals into your decisions, against displayed evidence; interactive for a person, --attest-blind is the recorded, disclosed escape; an agent ratifies under its own name with --agent <name> --for <person>, --list then --accept (runward ADR-0066, ADR-0082)

  report [options]                         write the delivery report an assessor reads alone (ADR-0064): one self-contained HTML, rendered from the same machine payload check --json publishes — computes nothing, works without a terminal, an account or runward installed

  compliance [options] [regime]            assemble a regime-framed evidence pack from the mission (deterministic, read-only; a readiness draft, never a compliance claim)

  -p, --path <path>     project directory

                        an analysis policy the mission pins, also read the
                        delivered code for the invariants it declares, never
                        running it (ADR-0118)
  --freeze              seal a green strict gate: hash the evidence into
                        runward/evidence-lock.json (implies --strict)
  --hooks               run operator hooks from runward/hooks.json around the
                        audit (opt-in)
  --coverage            advisory: report deliverable + decision-ratification
                        coverage (does not gate)

                        including <phase-id> (frame | architect | floor | govern
                        | handover), a prefix of the arc — a progress signal,
                        never the sole release gate (ADR-0053) (choices:
                        "frame", "architect", "floor", "govern", "handover")

                        its rows — mechanical (the default: at least one applied
                        row carries a pointer the gate opened and checked, else
                        exit 5) or traced (a green that rests on judgment alone,
                        accepted by name); a --through prefix requires traced
                        unless told otherwise (ADR-0114). Above them (ADR-0119):
                        re-derived (no applied row rests on a declaration, and
                        the declared territory is analysed) and attested (also,
                        every report a row cites is bound to this tree by a
                        signed run Statement of runward-run, ADR-0120; the
                        binding is re-derived by this command, the signature is
                        verified outside it); below the level asked, exit 5. It
                        lifts no gap: a row refused as requires-unmet, citing
                        another kind of evidence than its rule requires, stays
                        exit 1 under --require traced; its ways out are a report
                        of that kind, a deviated row, or the nature declared
                        uncarriable in an accepted ADR (ADR-0115) (choices:
                        "traced", "mechanical", "re-derived", "attested")
  --json                machine output: verdict, current gate, deliverable
                        states, conformance gaps, next step (stable contract,
                        for agent-driven runs; gaps.proposed and
                        gaps.unboundRows are already inside gaps.conformance,
                        never added to it, and so is gaps.analysis)
  --attest              emit the verdict as an unsigned in-toto attestation
                        (in-toto Statement wrapping --json; sign it yourself
                        under your own key)

                        (what its own .gitignore files do not ignore, read
                        without git) as a second subject; `verify` then names
                        each file changed, added or removed. The verdict does
                        not read it (ADR-0113)
  --sarif               emit the verdict as a SARIF 2.1.0 log (annotations on
                        the manifest rows; upload it yourself)
  --vsa                 emit the verdict as a SLSA Verification Summary
                        Attestation (needs --resource-uri; set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
                        to keep it byte-idempotent)
  --resource-uri <uri>  the artifact the VSA is about (a package, image or
                        release URI) — required with --vsa, never guessed
  --witness <file>      with --strict: also write the witness of the verdict to
                        <file> (runward-witness/1, specified at
                        https://github.com/stranxik/runward/blob/main/docs/spec/witness.md):
                        the facts it relied on, for a separate checker to
                        re-check; stdout and the exit code are unchanged
  --codequality <file>  also write the verdict as a Code Quality report
                        (CodeClimate-shaped JSON, GitLab's merge-request widget)
                        to <file>: one issue per cause, fingerprints stable
                        across runs; stdout and the exit code are unchanged
  --junit <file>        also write the verdict as a JUnit XML report to <file>
                        (no test is executed: one case per cause and one
                        `runward gate` case); runward refuses its own JUnit as
                        evidence; stdout and the exit code are unchanged
